Stephanie / team — quick technical read:

Summary: the targets are achievable, with caveats. See infra_impact_notes.md (attached) for details.

- Uptime: 99.95% for a Dedicated single-region cluster is our standard SLA for reserved capacity. To reach 99.99% consistently we need:
  * Active-passive multi-region configuration with automated failover (adds cross-region replication and DNS failover).
  * Dedicated hot-standby capacity (at least ~20% buffer) or guaranteed burst capacity.
  * Formal maintenance windows and runbook with RTO/RPO defined in SOW.
  * Estimated ops cost uplift: ~18-25% depending on model size and traffic profile.

- Latency (P95 <= 300ms for <=1k tokens):
  * Feasible on smaller LLMs and quantized execution on our NVL-class GPUs when requests are <1k tokens and KV caches are warm.
  * For larger models or cold caches, P95 will increase; we should add language that conditions the latency target on token size, model family, and a defined traffic profile.

Proposed order-form clause (engineering-friendly draft):
"Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain a monthly uptime of 99.99% for the Dedicated deployment described in the Order Form, provided Customer accepts the dedicated multi-region configuration described in the SOW and reserves the minimum capacity specified in Appendix A. Latency commitments (P95) are scoped to request size and workload profile; the parties shall agree a target model and token profile prior to go-live. Scheduled maintenance windows and documented failover procedures will be excluded from uptime calculations."

I'll attach infra_impact_notes.md with the configuration checklist and cost delta. Happy to sync with Ops for a short 30-min call with AtriumTech if they want finer detail.

—Marcus
